chunks: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Aswari narrated to us, saying: Makki ibn Ahmad ibn Sa'dawayh al-Burdha'i narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn Muhammad ibn al-Musayyib al-Bayhaqi informed us, saying: My grandfather narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abu Uways narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Dawud ibn Qays al-San'ani narrated to me, saying: Aflah ibn Kathir narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

That Jibra'il descended to him with this supplication from the heavens, and descended to him smiling and rejoicing, saying: 'Peace be upon you, O Muhammad.' He replied: 'And peace be upon you, O Jibra'il.' Then he said: 'Verily, Allah has sent a gift to you.' He asked: 'What is that gift, O Jibra'il?' He answered: 'Words from the Treasures of the Throne, by which Allah honors you.' He asked: 'What are they, O Jibra'il?'

He said: Say: 'O One who reveals beauty and hides ugliness, O One who does not punish the offender and does not tear the veil, O Most Great in Pardoning, O Best of the Overlookers, O All-Embracing in Forgiveness, O One who Opens His Hands in Mercy, O Hearer of all Whispers, O One to whom all Complaints are made, O Last Resort of the Fallen, O Noble One, O Possessor of Great Favor, O One who gives blessings before anyone deserves it, O our Lord, O our Master, O our Guardian, O Goal of our Desires, I beseech You, O Allah, not to make my being ugly by means of the Fire.'

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) asked: 'O Jibra'il, what is the reward for these words?' He said: 'So great! So great! The knowledge is cut off. Even if the angels of the seven heavens and the seven earths joined together to describe the reward for that until the Day of Judgment, they would not be able to describe even one part of a thousandth part.'

And when the servant says: 'O One who reveals beauty and hides ugliness,' Allah covers him with His Mercy in this world, and completely in the Hereafter. Allah covers him with a thousand veils in this world and the Hereafter. And when he says: 'O One who does not punish the offender and does not tear the veil,' Allah will not hold him accountable on the Day of Judgment, and will not tear his veil on the Day all veils are torn.

And when he says: 'O Most Great in Pardoning,' Allah forgives his sins even if his mistake is like the foam of the sea. And when he says: 'O Best of the Overlookers,' Allah overlooks for him even theft, drinking wine, and worldly terrors, and other major sins.

And when he says: 'O All-Embracing in Forgiveness,' Allah, the Mighty and High, opens for him seventy gates of Mercy, so he wades in the Mercy of Allah, the Mighty and High, until he departs this world. And when he says: 'O One who Opens His Hands in Mercy,' Allah opens His Hand of Mercy to him.

And when he says: 'O Hearer of all Whispers, O One to whom all Complaints are made,' Allah, the Mighty and High, gives him the reward of every afflicted one, every healthy one, every sick one, every blind one, every destitute one, and every poor one until the Day of Judgment.

And when he says: 'O Noble One,' Allah honors him with the honor of the prophets. And when he says: 'O Possessor of Great Favor,' Allah gives him on the Day of Judgment his desire and the desire of all creatures.

And when he says: 'O One who gives blessings before anyone deserves it,' Allah gives him reward equal to the number of those who thanked Him for His blessings. And when he says: 'O our Lord, O our Master, O our Guardian,' Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'My angels! Bear witness that I forgave him, and I gave him reward equal to the number of those I created in Paradise and Hell, the seven heavens, the seven earths, the sun, the moon, the stars, rain drops, types of creatures, mountains, pebbles, soil, and other than these, as well as the Empyrean and the Throne.'

And when he says: 'O our Guardian,' Allah fills his heart with faith. And when he says: 'O Goal of our Desires,' Allah gives him on the Day of Judgment his desire and the like of the desire of all creatures.

And when he says: 'I beseech You, O Allah, not to make my being ugly by means of the Fire,' the Supreme, may His glory be glorified, says: 'My servant has asked Me to free him from the Fire. My angels! Bear witness that I have freed him from the Fire, and I have freed his parents, his sisters, his brothers, his household, his children, and his neighbors. I accepted his intercession for a thousand men who deserved the Fire, and I saved them from it.'

Teach them, O Muhammad, to the pious, and do not teach them to the hypocrites, for it is a supplication granted to those who pronounce it, by the will of Allah. This is the supplication of the inhabitants of the Flourishing House, when they circumambulate it.

The Compiler of this book says: The proof that Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, is All-Knowing, Ever-Living, and All-Powerful in and of Himself—not by knowledge, power, and life that are other than Him—is that if He were All-Knowing by means of knowledge, His knowledge would not be free from one of two things: either it is eternal or created. If it is created, then He, glorified be His Praise, was without knowledge before its creation. This is an imperfect attribute, and every imperfection is caused, as we explained previously. If it is eternal, then it becomes necessary for other than Allah, the Mighty and High, to be eternal. This is infidelity by consensus. The same argument applies to the All-Powerful and His Omnipotence, and the Ever-Living and His Life. The proof that He, the Exalted, has always been All-Powerful, All-Knowing, and Ever-Living is that it has been established that He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful, and Ever-Living in and of Himself, and it is correct by evidence that He, the Mighty and High, is Eternal. And if He is so, then He has always been All-Knowing, as His Essence, which possesses knowledge, has always been. This indicates that He has always been All-Powerful and Ever-Living. Chapter: What is the Quran?

key_terms.الْبَيْتُ الْمَعُورُ: The Flourishing House, a celestial house whose inhabitants recite this supplication
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: Knowledge, discussed as an eternal attribute of Allah in Himself
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقُونَ: Hypocrites, to whom the supplication should not be taught
key_terms.جِبْرِئِيلُ: Gabriel, the archangel who delivered the supplication
key_terms.صِفَاتُ النُّقْصِ: Attributes of imperfection, used in the theological proof of divine unity
key_terms.كُنُوزُ الْعَرْشِ: Treasures of the Throne, indicating the high status of the words

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and rewards of the supplication revealed by Jibra'il to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* presents a profound supplication revealed by Jibra’il, emphasizing Allah’s attributes of beauty, concealment of faults, and boundless mercy, with specific rewards linked to each phrase. The compiler uses this narrative to support his theological argument for the eternity of Allah’s essential attributes (Knowledge, Power, Life), distinguishing them from created attributes to affirm divine unity. It serves as both a devotional guide for believers and a doctrinal proof in Shia scholastic theology.
